title: Air Ticket Fare Brands: Bookings Held at the Same Time and Duplicate Itineraries
content:
A traveller may hold any number of air bookings at the same time. No limit is placed on how many bookings sold under Air Ticket Fare Brands stand in one traveller's name at once, and each booking carries its own fare brand, its own money and its own terms.

**Each booking is read on its own.** The fare brand recorded on a booking governs that booking and no other, and the amounts collected on it are that booking's amounts.

**Duplicate itineraries.** Two bookings for the same traveller, on the same routing and for the same departure date are treated as a duplicate. Where that is the reading, the later booking is opened, and it is then referred for duplicate review before it is ticketed. The ground is that airlines refuse duplicate tickets in one name.

The three particulars are read together:

|Same traveller|Same routing|Same departure date|Reading|
|---|---|---|---|
|yes|yes|yes|a duplicate: the later booking is opened, then referred for duplicate review before it is ticketed|
|yes|yes|no|the duplicate reading is not engaged on these particulars|
|yes|no|yes|the duplicate reading is not engaged on these particulars|
|no|yes|yes|the duplicate reading is not engaged on these particulars|

**No aggregation.** Nothing in this charter aggregates the terms of two bookings. A benefit earned on one booking is never spent on another, except through the travel-credit account, which is governed separately.
